correctness.rationale: For Φpq the root order pq forces a period divisor of pq. The integral cokernel of X^p−1 is killed by q because ΦpqΦq=Φq(X^p), and reducing modulo q yields precisely Fq[X]/Φp(X), dimension p−1 since p≠q. Hence p−1 Smith entries q; exchanging primes gives q−1 entries p. Fixed points modulo m are gcd(q,m)^(p−1) and gcd(p,m)^(q−1). The identity Φpq(1)=1 gives F1=1 and C^pq=I gives Fpq=m^d. Inclusion-exclusion yields every integer cycle count. Five independently exhaustive state enumerations corroborate but do not replace the general proof; modulus one and prime-divisibility boundaries checked.

value.rationale: A complete all-modulus orbit census for the first cyclotomic index containing two distinct odd prime factors extends the arithmetic dynamics setting beyond the previously understood prime-power case. The two complementary finite torsion groups control every short orbit, distinguish whether p or q divides the modulus, and yield exact multiplicities without enumerating exponentially many states. This is a natural structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite instance.
